packageMeta.name: 208design high-fi walkthrough handoff
notes: Pages 2, 3, and 4 are tab states inside the root app shell rather than standalone routes.
The portfolio implementation should use screenshots, hotspots, and guided mock transitions instead of backend-connected interactions.
The design requirement ids in this package are inferred from the frontend UI and interaction logic.

functions.routeBehavior: Open the root app and tap Album in the bottom navigation.
functions.uiPurpose: Show photo-based family updates, attach short pet notes, and support lightweight acknowledgement through reactions.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: No extra action after opening the tab.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the family album overview cards as the entry state.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Tap a member card such as Mom.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the member-specific album detail with the main image and reaction launcher.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Open a member album, tap the reaction launcher, and choose an emoji.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the selected reaction and visible feedback state.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Open Grace's album and expand the summary card.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the recap/feedback layer for multiple pet notes.

tourSteps.tooltipBody: The overview uses large preview cards so each family member's recent update can be recognised before opening a detail view.
Each photo can receive a lightweight reaction, allowing family members to respond without composing a full message.
tourSteps.mockResult: The image enters a reaction-selection state.

tourSteps.tooltipBody: After selection, the chosen emoji appears directly on the image and the reacting family member is shown below.
tourSteps.suggestedAction: Notice the reaction marker and name badge
tourSteps.mockResult: The photo now carries a visible gentle response.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Pet notes become a compact recap
tourSteps.tooltipBody: The summary card turns multiple short captions into a brief narrative, helping the viewer recover context quickly.
tourSteps.mockResult: Several updates are condensed into one readable recap.

functions.routeBehavior: Open the root app and tap Jar in the bottom navigation.
functions.functionTitle: Mood Jar with Graduated Sharing Controls
functions.uiPurpose: Support quick daily mood logging, explicit privacy control, and bounded family care responses.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: No extra action after opening the tab.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the privacy-first jar entry state.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Tap the plus button to open the mood editor.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the mood picker and share controls.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Switch to a family account view and scroll to the shared jar area.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the shared-result visibility layer for family members.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: In a family account view, tap a care reaction such as Hug.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the visible family-feedback state after a care response.

tourSteps.tooltipBody: The jar invites a quick emotional check-in rather than a long written disclosure.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Use a constrained visual mood vocabulary
tourSteps.tooltipBody: A fixed set of mood beads allows the user to communicate state quickly with less cognitive load.
tourSteps.mockResult: The selected mood becomes the day's check-in.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Control how much family can see
tourSteps.tooltipBody: Private, Soft Share, and Full Share create explicit thresholds between self-tracking and family awareness.
tourSteps.mockResult: Only the permitted level of information is shared beyond the private calendar.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Shared beads are filtered before they reach family
tourSteps.tooltipBody: Only entries that pass the chosen share threshold appear in the shared jar and shared-status view.
tourSteps.suggestedAction: Notice the shared jar and status card
tourSteps.mockResult: The viewer understands the difference between private tracking and family awareness.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Family responses stay gentle and bounded
tourSteps.tooltipBody: Relatives can reply with small care gestures such as a hug, tea, or pet response.
tourSteps.mockResult: A short confirmation message appears beneath the shared-status card.

functions.routeBehavior: Open the root app and tap Echo in the bottom navigation.
functions.uiPurpose: Turn repeated small interactions into a weekly recap, a keepsake interaction, and a reflective summary state.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: No extra action after opening the tab.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the recap board as the entry state.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Move to the keepsake board using the arrow controls.
screenshots.purpose: Shows the main interaction board before the reveal.

screenshots.preCaptureAction: Capture the strongest final recap or keepsake-summary state available from the frontend-only flow.
screenshots.purpose: Provides the final reflective summary image for the walkthrough.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Review the week as a single calm recap
tourSteps.tooltipBody: The recap board condenses several forms of family interaction into one readable weekly story.
tourSteps.suggestedAction: Notice the recap text and metric tiles
tourSteps.mockResult: The weekly pattern is visible at a glance.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Turn collected activity into a keepsake
tourSteps.tooltipBody: The keepsake board reframes repeated small actions as cumulative progress and offers a clear reveal action.
tourSteps.mockResult: The walkthrough moves to the final reward state.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: Reflection continues through lightweight pet prompts
tourSteps.tooltipBody: Short reply chips allow the user to revisit the recap conversationally without leaving the reflection surface.
tourSteps.mockResult: The pet response changes to a different reflective prompt.

tourSteps.tooltipTitle: The reward is presented as a memory object
tourSteps.tooltipBody: The final state names the keepsake, explains why it was unlocked, and frames it as a meaningful weekly outcome.
tourSteps.mockResult: The week's small traces are presented as a cumulative family memory.

designRequirementAlignment.name: Gentle asynchronous family connection
designRequirementAlignment.description: Support low-pressure family contact through short, lightweight, asynchronous interactions.
uiEvidence: Weekly Echo recap boards and pet reply chips
designRequirementAlignment.portfolioWording: The interface prioritises gentle asynchronous family connection by turning updates into short, low-pressure touchpoints rather than demanding real-time conversation.

designRequirementAlignment.name: Graduated privacy and user control
designRequirementAlignment.description: Let the student decide what remains private and what becomes visible to family.
uiEvidence: Private, Soft Share, and Full Share options
shared status card visible in family view
designRequirementAlignment.portfolioWording: The mood-sharing flow separates private self-tracking from family-visible awareness through explicit share thresholds.

designRequirementAlignment.name: Lightweight acknowledgement and care feedback
designRequirementAlignment.description: Provide bounded response mechanisms that feel supportive without requiring long messages.
uiEvidence: Hug, Tea, and Pet responses in Jar
Summary, More, and Thanks quick replies in Weekly Echo
designRequirementAlignment.portfolioWording: Response mechanisms are intentionally lightweight, allowing acknowledgement and care without increasing communication pressure.

designRequirementAlignment.name: Cumulative reflection and memory-making
designRequirementAlignment.description: Transform scattered daily traces into readable summaries and longer-lived keepsakes.
uiEvidence: Weekly Echo recap board and keepsake reveal
designRequirementAlignment.portfolioWording: Small daily traces are accumulated into summaries, shared states, and keepsake rewards so that interaction produces longer-term meaning.
